events.title: Joan of Arc Arrives at Orléans
events.description: Joan of Arc, a teenage peasant girl who said she was guided by divine visions, reached the besieged city of Orléans. She came at the head of a French relief force. Her arrival lifted the spirits of the defenders after months of English siege.
events.significance: Her arrival began the campaign that broke the siege within days. It became a turning point in the Hundred Years' War and made Joan a national symbol of France.

events.title: Captain James Cook Lands at Botany Bay
events.description: The British explorer James Cook brought HMS Endeavour into a wide bay on Australia's southeastern coast and went ashore. The bay was later named Botany Bay for the many new plant species gathered there by the expedition's naturalists.
events.significance: The landing was the start of sustained British contact with Australia's east coast. It shaped the later colonization of the continent and the history of its Indigenous peoples.

events.title: Dachau Is Liberated
events.description: Soldiers of the U.S. Seventh Army entered Dachau, the first Nazi concentration camp, near Munich. They found thousands of emaciated survivors and many dead. The discovery shocked the troops and the world.
events.significance: The liberation of Dachau became one of the defining moments in the world's reckoning with the Holocaust. It left lasting evidence of Nazi crimes.

events.title: Hitler Marries Eva Braun in the Führerbunker
events.description: As Soviet forces closed in on Berlin, Adolf Hitler married his longtime partner Eva Braun in a brief ceremony in his underground bunker. He also named Admiral Karl Dönitz as his successor. The couple died by suicide the next day.
events.significance: The wedding and Hitler's succession arrangements came just before the collapse of Nazi Germany. Within days the war in Europe was effectively over.
